history.name: History
history.content: History as Minor in Semester 4 is the Mughal India paper, tracing the state from expansion and ideology through administration, alliances and religion to art. The syllabus is arranged in four units across ten lessons, starting with technology and techniques of consolidation, the nature of the Mughal state, Chaghatai imperial ideology seen in the Jahangirnama, and the evolution of administration from Akbar to Aurangzeb through Mansabdari, Jagirdari, Zabt and Jaziya. It then moves to Mughal–Rajput political alliances and religious patterns between 1550 and 1700, followed by the rise of Shivaji and the Marathas and the relationship between the Mughal state and the Sikhs. A DU-specific feature is that the final unit examines the Taj Mahal and Red Fort for architecture and Jahangir and Shah Jahan for painting as case studies of state patronage, not as isolated art history. Students often lose marks by writing generic dynastic narratives without anchoring answers to the lesson headings — for instance, listing Mansabdari features without showing how it changed between Akbar and Aurangzeb as Lesson 4 frames it.

economics.name: Economics
economics.content: Introductory Statistics for Economics (BA Hons ECON003, Semester I) gives you the descriptive and probabilistic foundation that every later statistics and econometrics paper assumes. The course is organised in five units — introduction with population-sample distinction and measures of location and variability, elementary probability, random variables and their distributions, special distributions, and random sampling with jointly distributed variables including covariance and correlation. In the special-distributions unit you cover Uniform, Binomial, Exponential, Poisson, Hypergeometric and Normal distributions, with Bernoulli and Geometric explicitly included via Devore Chapters 3 and 4. A DU-specific detail recorded in the Department of Economics meeting minutes is the 90-mark end-semester pattern: Units 1–2 together carry 20 marks with a choice to attempt 2 of 3 questions, Unit 3 carries 20, Unit 4 carries 30 with three compulsory 10-mark questions, and Unit 5 carries 20, with no sub-part below 5 marks and Devore as the principal text. The minutes also direct that stem-and-leaf display and the Poisson–Exponential relation are not to be examined and that double integration for joint continuous variables should be kept simple. Because the content feels mechanical, students most often lose marks on presentation rules they ignore — not answering each section contiguously from a new page and not rounding intermediate calculations to three decimals and final answers to two.

evs-theory-into-practice-i.name: EVS Theory into Practice I
evs-theory-into-practice-i.content: EVS: Theory into Practice I is DU's compulsory 2-credit AEC for Year 1 — you study four units across one semester, not seven: Introduction to Environmental Studies, Ecosystems, Natural Resources, and Environmental Pollution. You move from the multidisciplinary nature of environment and sustainability through ecosystem structure and energy flow to land, water and energy resources with Indian cases like Sardar Sarovar and Chipko, then to air, water and solid-waste pollution with cases like Ganga Action Plan and Delhi air pollution. DU runs this as 1 lecture + 1 practical hour per week (2 credits total), and the practical is not optional — your file includes SDG analysis, Google Earth ecosystem mapping, biodiversity-park visits and AQI or compost work that counts as the second credit. Most students slip by writing long textbook paragraphs without a diagram or data point and by skipping the case-study name and one takeaway line. One neat ecological pyramid or nutrient-cycle sketch with two case names fetches more marks than two extra pages of theory.

financial-literacy.name: Financial Literacy
financial-literacy.content: Financial Literacy is DU's 2-credit VAC that teaches you personal finance in four short blocks: Financial Planning and Financial Products (saving, time value of money, spending discipline), Banking and Digital Payment, Investment Planning and Management (including life and medical insurance), and Personal Tax. As of 2026, DU's official syllabus still lists exactly what you use daily — debit/ATM and credit cards, net banking and UPI, digital wallets, plus security against Ponzi schemes and online frauds, and e-filing for tax — so the paper ages with your phone, not your textbook. DU counts it as 1 lecture + 1 practical hour per week and expects a practical file: banking product comparison, a dummy stock portfolio, an investment budget that balances return and tax, a dummy ITR, and even a financial-literacy survey of 25 people. Students lose the most marks on the numericals (time value of money, tax deductions) and by writing definitions of UPI without the precaution or comparison the syllabus asks for. Solving last year's numbers and keeping one page per unit with a formula and a live-bank example is how you turn a theory paper into a scoring one.

delhi-through-the-ages.name: Delhi Through the Ages
delhi-through-the-ages.content: Delhi Through the Ages (GE-1) is History's 4-credit GE that traces Delhi from its early landscape to the eighteenth century in four units, not as one long chronology. You start with Ancient Delhi and its adjoining sites — Indraprastha-Hastinapur-Panipat-Tilpat, Ashokan Edicts, the Mehrauli Iron Pillar and Lalkot — then compare two Sultanate cities of your choice among Anangpur Fort, Siri, Tughlaqabad, Firuzabad and others, before moving to Humayun's Garden Tomb and the morphology of Shahjahanabad and finally to 18th-century political and social change in the city. DU offers it as 3 lectures + 1 tutorial each week and spreads the units over 12 + 16 + 16 + 16 hours with encouraged field trips to the sites you write about. Students lose marks by mixing up the Sultanate cities and by writing a generic 'Delhi history' without anchoring each answer to a specific monument, edict or traveller account from the reading list. One timeline, two case studies prepared with a plan sketch, and a Sufi or merchant example is what turns a descriptive answer into a high-scoring one.

political-science.name: Political Science
political-science.content: Political Science (Hons) as a Core under UGCF 2022 builds through 4-credit DSC papers each semester; in Semester 8 — the syllabus verified for 2025-26 — the Core is DSC-20 Development Process and Social Movements in Contemporary India, a 4-credit (3 lecture +1 tutorial) paper on page 3 of the official PDF. The PDF organises it into four Units: Unit I Development Process since Independence (state and planning, liberalisation and reforms, and recent monetary/fiscal trends including GST), Unit II Industrial Development Strategy and its impact on organised/unorganised labour and the new middle class, Unit III Agrarian Development Strategy (land reforms, Green Revolution and the agrarian crisis since the 1990s with land acquisition), and Unit IV Social Movements, Migration and Development (tribal, farmers, Dalit, women's and civil-rights movements). A DU-specific detail examiners expect is that the PDF prints no fixed 75/25 split — it closes each paper with “Examination scheme and mode shall be as prescribed by the Examination Branch … from time to time” — so credits and the tutorial component matter more than an assumed marks table. Students lose marks because the Essential Readings list runs to 30-plus sources per Unit and questions reward linking planning to dispossession — writing GST or Green Revolution without the movement or migration link reads as incomplete as taught in 2025-26.

b-com-hons.name: B.Com (Hons)
b-com-hons.content: B.Com (Hons) under UGCF/NEP 2022 is a 4-credit DSC per semester; in Semester 8 — the syllabus verified for 2025-26 — students take either DSC-8.1 The Economy of Bharat or DSC-8.2 Financial Technology and Analytics, each 4 credits (3 lecture +1 tutorial) on page 3 of the official PDF. DSC-8.1 is organised into four Units: Unit 1 on growth and development with Kautilya's Arthashastra, HDI, Temple Economy and sustainability tools like Net Zero and Carbon Credit Trading; Unit 2 on the Economy of Bharat from Planning Commission to NITI Aayog with regional imbalances, multidimensional poverty, demographics and the gig economy. Units 3 and 4 cover agriculture and industry (four agricultural revolutions, digital agriculture and drones, MSMEs, disinvestment and CPSE CSR) and services plus external sector (services share in GDP, Make in India and Atma Nirbhar Bharat, trade since 1991, Balance of Payments and Viksit Bharat strategies). A DU-specific rule printed on page 3 is that students who have already studied GE Indian Economy (ECON030) or Sectoral Issues in Indian Economy (ECON059) may not opt for DSC-8.1 and must take FinTech instead — colleges enforce this at form fill. Students lose marks because the Exercises ask for a statistical profile and evaluation of BOP or disinvestment data, not textbook definitions, and writing Kautilya or Green Revolution without a table, trend or policy link leaves the 1-tutorial component under-answered as taught in 2025-26.

advanced-spreadsheets-tools.name: Advanced Spreadsheets Tools
advanced-spreadsheets-tools.content: Advanced Spreadsheets Tools is a 2-credit SEC (0 lecture +0 tutorial +2 practical, Theme 17 Sl.88) under UGCF 2022, offered in Semesters 3–5 and verified for 2025-26 as a fully practical paper. The official PDF organises it in four timed blocks: Unit 1 Excel Advanced Techniques (3 weeks) — templates, Standard Deviation/Variance/Coefficient of Variation, Data Validation, lookup/power/array formulae, advanced range names, Goal Seek/Data Tables/Scenario Manager and the Data Analysis ToolPak with Solver and regression for projection; Unit 2 Excel Interactivity and Automation (4 weeks) — Index/Match, Offset, dynamic charting, database/text/error functions, form controls and basic VBA with absolute/relative macros, loops and UserForms. Units 3 and 4 complete it: Unit 3 Introduction to VBA (4 weeks) on conditional formatting, charts that inspire (Waterfall, Thermometer, Histogram), Slicers, Sparklines and graphics tricks, and Unit 4 Data Analysis and Decision-Making (4 weeks) on external data, advanced PivotTables, PowerPivot/Power Query, dashboards and applied sheets for loan/lease, ratio/payroll, NPV/IRR, breakeven and optimisation. A DU-specific verified detail is the printed marking scheme on page 3: Total 100 — Internal Assessment 25, Practical Exam (Internal) 25, End Semester University Exam 50 — with Internal Assessment left to faculty. Students lose marks because they revise by reading PDFs; the paper is marked on file work and viva, and a workbook without Ctrl+~ formula views, without a working Goal Seek or Solver model, or without a PivotTable-driven dashboard scores low even if definitions are memorised as taught in 2025-26.

digital-marketing.name: Digital Marketing
digital-marketing.content: Digital Marketing is a 2-credit SEC (0 lecture +0 tutorial +2 practical, Theme 17 Sl.96, UPC 2926000002) under UGCF 2022, offered to BA/BSc/BCom in Semesters 3–5 and verified for 2025-26 as a practice-oriented paper. The official syllabus divides into four blocks: Unit 1 Marketing in the Digital World (3 weeks) — digital marketing concept and how it differs from traditional, the four channel buckets (Intent-Based SEO/Search Advertising, Brand-Based Display, Community-Based Social Media, plus Affiliate/Email/Content/Mobile), Customer Value Journey 5As Framework and the Ozone O3 concept; Unit 2 Content and Email Marketing (2 weeks) — step-by-step content strategy and email types with best practices. Units 3 and 4 are the large ones: Unit 3 Social Media and Display Marketing (5 weeks) — building a social strategy for Facebook/LinkedIn/YouTube and the full display process (customer/publisher/objectives, budget/media/ad formats/ad copy); Unit 4 Search Engine Marketing (5 weeks) — how search engines and SERP positioning work, DMI's 5P Model, SEO on-page (keyword research, sitemaps, structured markup) and off-page (link building, black vs white hat), and Search Advertising/PPC (Google Ads account, campaign architecture, targeting, bid strategy). A DU-specific verified detail is the same 100-mark split printed on page 3: Internal Assessment 25, Practical Exam (Internal) 25, End Semester University Exam 50. Students find it difficult because the paper mixes vocabulary (SERP, PPC, black-hat) with a hands-on Google Ads setup; writing definitions for SEO without showing on-page vs off-page steps or a dummy campaign structure is where most lose marks as taught in 2025-26.

digital-empowerment.name: Digital Empowerment
digital-empowerment.content: As notified in the UGCF 2022 VAC pool and taught in 2025-26, Digital Empowerment is a 2-credit VAC (1 lecture +1 practical) that moves in four blocks: Digital inclusion and the Vision of Digital India — DigiLocker, E-Hospitals, e-Pathshala, BHIM, e-Kranti and portals for RTI, health, finance and tax filing — then Communication and Collaboration (email, blogs, social media, file-sharing, messaging and video conferencing), then Safe and Secure Cyberspace (privacy, data breach, cyber attacks, Blockchain and government security initiatives) and finally Ethical Issues including netiquettes. A DU-specific requirement on page 12 that most students miss is the 15-week practical: interactive demonstrations, workshops on Digital India services, outreach to street vendors, domestic help, security guards and senior citizens, and team projects on education, health, farming and financial inclusion. The paper feels easy, so students cram definitions and write paragraphs where the syllabus asks for steps — for example, exact steps to collaborate on Drive or secure a transaction.

yoga-philosophy-and-practice.name: Yoga: Philosophy & Practice
yoga-philosophy-and-practice.content: As notified in the same UGCF 2022 VAC notification and taught in 2025-26, Yoga: Philosophy and Practice is a 2-credit VAC (1 lecture +1 practical) with three theory blocks: Yoga — Asana, Pranayama and Dhyana (history, significance of asana, effect of pranayama, importance of dhyana), Patanjali’s Yogasutra and Chakra (summary plus first and second sutras and psychic chakras), and Understanding Asana and Pranayama (basics, Surya Namaskar and Nadi Shodhana). The verified 15-week practical is prescriptive: Surya Namaskar, selected asana and pranayama, eye-relaxation in 7 steps and neck in 4 steps, concentration on bhrumadhya, and a project report on just 15 minutes of daily breath observation. Because the title says “Philosophy”, students prepare only sutra meanings and lose marks where the syllabus actually awards them — writing Surya Namaskar steps in order, naming Nadi Shodhana correctly, and showing the 7/4-step relaxation precisely as prescribed.

evs-theory-into-practice-ii.name: EVS Theory into Practice II
evs-theory-into-practice-ii.content: The second-year AEC Environmental Science: Theory into Practice — II, as notified in September 2023 under UGCF 2022 and taught in 2025-26, is a 2-credit course (1 hour theory +2 hours practical, 3 hours total) that continues from Year 1 with three units: Global Environmental Issues and Policies, Biodiversity and Conservation, and Human Communities and the Environment. Verified on pages 120–121, Unit V covers climate change, global warming, ozone and acid rain plus Earth Summit, UNFCCC, Montreal, Kyoto, CBD, Ramsar and Indian laws from the Wildlife Protection Act 1972 to the Forest Rights Act 2006; Unit VI spans India’s mega-biodiversity, IUCN Red List, threats and in-situ/ex-situ strategies including Project Tiger and Silent Valley; Unit VII links population, resettlement, Chipko/Appiko/Narmada movements, the National Green Tribunal and environmental ethics. The DU-specific weight is the 15-week practical outreach — temperature-trend mapping, NDC reviews, Model UNFCCC and Green Tribunal moot courts, carbon-footprint and a 3-SDG proposal with PowerPoint.

hindi-bhasha-sampreshan-aur-sanchar.name: Hindi Bhasha: Sampreshan aur Sanchar
hindi-bhasha-sampreshan-aur-sanchar.content: Hindi Bhasha: Sampreshan aur Sanchar — Hindi – Ka in the DU AEC pool as notified in February 2023 and taught in 2025-26 — is the 2-credit AEC-1 for students who studied Hindi till Class 12 (2 lecture hours, Department of Hindi). Its 15-week syllabus is deliberately narrow: Ikai 1 covers sampreshan ki avdharana, prakriya, ayam and the sampreshan-sanchar link (weeks 1–7), while Ikai 2 moves to application — sampreshan ke prakar, a survey-based report on topics like Corona and mental health, awareness campaigns or waste disposal, plus anuchedh, samvad, diary, blog and sampadakiya lekhan (weeks 8–15). A DU-specific detail verified on page 78 is the assessment split: total 50 marks, with 38 for the written exam and 12 for internal assessment, not the 70 or 90 students expect from core papers.

indian-economy.name: Indian Economy
indian-economy.content: Indian Economy — ECON030, listed as GE-6 in the UGCF 2022 common pool and offered in even semesters II/IV/VI/VIII as taught in 2025-26 — is a 4-credit GE (3 lectures +1 tutorial, no practical, Class XII pass, no prerequisite) that is policy-and-evidence driven, not a lighter version of Honours Micro. The verified syllabus compresses into five blocks of about nine hours each: historical overview since Independence, growth and structural change, the Indian economy in comparative perspective, key issues of poverty, inequality, education, health and gender, and agriculture, industry, services and international trade. A DU-specific detail on page 12 is that the course cites research databases and readings — Balakrishnan, Rakshit, Goyal, Ghate, Rakesh Mohan on the “Big Push” and the Rangarajan poverty report — rather than textbook diagrams.

business-management-organisation.name: Business Management / Organisation
business-management-organisation.content: Business Organisation — BCH: GE-1.1 in the Commerce common pool as notified in 2022 and offered in 2025-26 — is a 4-credit generic elective (3 lectures +1 tutorial) that, in the verified CDN syllabus, runs five units of 12 hours each: Introduction (business as a system, ethics and social responsibility), Business Enterprises (sole proprietorship through MNC plus LLP, one-person company and mergers/takeovers), Business Environment (internal/external dimensions and SWOT/ETOP), Entrepreneurship (the entrepreneur-enterprise link and Skill India, Startup India, Make in India and glocalisation) and Contemporary Issues (learning organisations, workforce diversity, franchising, outsourcing, e-commerce, sustainability and digitalisation). A DU-specific assessment on page 2 is the practical: you are given a scenario — capital, liability and scale — and must choose a business form and justify it, plus a SWOT for a chosen firm.

b-sc-hons-biological-sciences.name: B.Sc. (Hons) Biological Sciences
b-sc-hons-biological-sciences.content: B.Sc. (Hons) Biological Sciences at Delhi University is an integrated life-sciences degree that combines botany, zoology and chemistry rather than a single discipline. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 programme structure lists Sem 1 DSCs as Basic concepts of Biomolecules (UPC 6792011101), Photobiology (6792011102) and Diversity in Life forms I (6792011103), each 4 credits with a 2-theory + 2-practical split. The course then moves through Cell Biology and Diversity of Life Forms-II in Sem 2 to Functional Ecology, Metabolism, Physiology and later Molecular Biology and Evolution in Sem 5-6. Students typically find it demanding because three streams are examined together and lose marks when they treat practicals — specimen identification, biomolecule tests and field observations — as secondary to theory.

b-sc-hons-botany.name: B.Sc. (Hons) Botany
b-sc-hons-botany.content: B.Sc. (Hons) Botany at Delhi University progresses from plant diversity and cell structure to systematics, ecology, physiology and biotechnology. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 programme lists 18 DSCs across six semesters; Sem 1 opens with Plant Diversity and Evolution (BOT-DSC-1, UPC 2162011101), Cell Biology: Organelles and Biomolecules (BOT-DSC-2, 2162011102) and Basic Laboratory and Field Skills in Plant Biology (2162011103), each 4 credits with a 2-theory + 2-practical split. Later semesters cover Phycology, Bryophytes-Pteridophytes-Gymnosperms, Genetics, Mycology, Ecology and Molecular Biology. Students often lose marks on practical records, herbarium preparation and labelled diagrams where original observation and correct nomenclature matter more than memorised text.

b-sc-hons-chemistry.name: B.Sc. (Hons) Chemistry
b-sc-hons-chemistry.content: B.Sc. (Hons) Chemistry at Delhi University follows the classic inorganic, organic and physical rotation in every semester. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 programme shows Sem 1 DSCs as Atomic Structure and Chemical Bonding - Inorganic I (UPC 2172011101, 3 theory + 1 practical), Basic Concepts and Aliphatic Hydrocarbons - Organic I (2172011102, 3T+1P) and Gaseous and Liquid State - Physical I (2172011103, 2T+2P). The sequence continues with s- and p-block, thermodynamics and equilibrium through Sem 2-3, and later quantum chemistry and spectroscopy in Sem 5-6. Students most often lose marks on reaction mechanisms, numerical problems and practical titrations where steps and calculations must be shown exactly as taught.

b-sc-hons-computer-science.name: B.Sc. (Hons) Computer Science
b-sc-hons-computer-science.content: B.Sc. (Hons) Computer Science at Delhi University is code-heavy from the first semester and builds toward systems and AI. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 structure lists Sem 1 DSCs as Object Oriented Programming using Python (UPC 2342011104), Computer System Architecture (2342011102) and Mathematics for Computing (2342011103), each 4 credits (3 theory + 1 practical). Sem 2-4 continue with C++, Discrete Structures, Data Structures, Operating Systems, Algorithms, DBMS and Computer Networks, while Sem 5-6 add Machine Learning, Theory of Computation and Deep Learning. Students tend to lose marks when they skip practical file correctness, time complexity analysis or precise definitions that examiners expect verbatim.

b-sc-hons-environmental-science.name: B.Sc. (Hons) Environmental Science
b-sc-hons-environmental-science.content: B.Sc. (Hons) Environmental Science at Delhi University is deliberately interdisciplinary, linking earth, chemistry, physics and ecology. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 programme lists Sem 1 DSCs as Environmental and Earth Surface Processes (UPC 2182011101), Environmental Physics (2182011102) and Environmental Chemistry (2182011103), each 4 credits (2 theory + 2 practical). Later semesters cover Water, Land and Soil, Ecosystems, Environmental Biotechnology, Atmosphere and Climate Change, and finally Biodiversity, Pollution and Urban Ecosystems. The breadth is the difficulty: students often lose marks when they write generic answers without data, case references or correct practical methodology for field and lab work.

b-sc-hons-food-technology.name: B.Sc. (Hons) Food Technology
b-sc-hons-food-technology.content: B.Sc. (Hons) Food Technology at Delhi University applies chemistry, microbiology and engineering to food processing, preservation and safety. As of 2026, the notified UGCF 2022 syllabi for Semesters 4-6 (DU notification dated 04.01.2024, Appendix-II-A, Ordinance V (2-A)) include DSC FT10 Food Quality Management as a 4-credit paper (3 theory + 1 practical) with three theory units: Introduction to Food Quality, Approaches to Food Quality Management, and Food Quality Management during production. The programme also runs through Fundamentals of Food Technology in Sem 1 to Technology of Food Preservation, Fruits-Vegetables and Dairy-Seafood (Sem 2-3) and onward to Food Engineering and Food Chemistry. Students often lose marks when they neglect precise practical protocols — HACCP plans, quality inspection of grains/pulses, and sensory evaluation sheets — where examiners check steps, not just conclusions.

b-sc-hons-geology.name: B.Sc. (Hons) Geology
b-sc-hons-geology.content: B.Sc. (Hons) Geology at Delhi University moves from earth systems and minerals to structural, igneous, palaeontological and applied geology. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 structure lists Sem 1 DSCs as Earth System Science (UPC 2192011101), Mineral Science (2192011102) and Concepts of Stratigraphy (2192011103), each 4 credits (3 theory + 1 practical). Later semesters cover Structural Geology, Igneous Petrology, Palaeontology, Sedimentary and Metamorphic Geology, Hydrogeology and Economic Geology. Students often lose marks on field-based papers — Geological Mapping (2T+2P in Sem 5) and Remote Sensing & GIS — where map work, cross-sections and neat field records are assessed strictly.

b-sc-hons-home-science.name: B.Sc. (Hons) Home Science
b-sc-hons-home-science.content: B.Sc. (Hons) Home Science at Delhi University spans five domains — human development, food and nutrition, textiles, resource management and communication — in every year. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 programme lists Sem 1 DSCs as Human Development I: The Early Years (UPC 2202011101), Food Science and Nutrition (2202011102) and Communication Concepts and Theories (2202011103), each 4 credits (3 theory + 1 practical), except Life Science/Physical Science papers which carry 2T+2P. The course then cycles through Fashion Studies, Nutrition: Life Cycle Approach, Textile Science and Dietetics and Public Health Nutrition. Its breadth is the challenge: students often lose marks by writing thin answers outside their favourite domain and by under-preparing the practical files that carry a full credit in most DSCs.

b-sc-hons-physics.name: B.Sc. (Hons) Physics
b-sc-hons-physics.content: B.Sc. (Hons) Physics at Delhi University is built around mathematical physics, mechanics, electricity and modern physics with a strong laboratory component. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 programme lists Sem 1 DSCs as Mathematical Physics I (UPC 2222011101, 3 theory + 1 practical), Mechanics (2222011102, 3T+1P) and Waves and Oscillations (2222011103, 2T+2P). The notification dated 12.01.2026 also revises Mathematical Physics-II and Thermal Physics within the same framework. Later semesters cover Modern Physics, Solid State, Electromagnetic Theory, Quantum Mechanics and Statistical Mechanics. Students often lose marks on derivations, dimensional analysis and practical error analysis where steps and units are scored, not just the final answer.

b-sc-hons-statistics.name: B.Sc. (Hons) Statistics
b-sc-hons-statistics.content: B.Sc. (Hons) Statistics at Delhi University blends probability theory, statistical methods and mathematics from the first semester. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 programme lists Sem 1 DSCs as Descriptive Statistics (UPC 2372011101), Introduction to Probability (2372011102) and Calculus (2372011103), each 4 credits (3 theory + 1 practical). Sem 2-3 move to Probability Distributions, Applied Statistics and Sample Surveys, while Sem 5-6 cover Estimation, Linear Models, Testing, Design and Econometrics. Students often lose marks on derivations of distributions, correct use of formulae and interpretation of practical outputs where examiners expect stepwise working and proper notation.

b-sc-hons-zoology.name: B.Sc. (Hons) Zoology
b-sc-hons-zoology.content: B.Sc. (Hons) Zoology at Delhi University starts with non-chordates and cell biology and progresses to physiology, genetics and biotechnology. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 programme lists Sem 1 DSCs as Nonchordata – Protists to Pseudocoelomates (UPC 2232011101), Biology of Cell: Structure and Function (2232013502) and Concept of Ecology (2232012303), each 4 credits (2 theory + 2 practical). Sem 2-4 then cover Coelomates, Human Physiology, Diversity of Chordates, Biochemistry and Developmental Biology. Students often lose marks on labelled diagrams, classification characters and practical spotting where neatness, correct terminology and original observation are scored.

baprog.name: BAprog
baprog.content: BA Programme at Delhi University is a multidisciplinary degree where students pursue two disciplines as majors/minors rather than a single honours. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 structure for BA (Prog) with English as Major shows Sem 1 DSCs as Introduction to Literary Studies (UPC 2032201101, 4 credits 3T+1T) and Indian Classical Literature (2032201102). The same pattern continues to 18th Century Literature in Sem 2 and Romantic and Victorian Literature in Sem 3, while other combinations like Sociology follow a parallel table with An Invitation to Sociology (2302201101) and Sociology of India. This dual-discipline load is where students often lose marks: answers must match the specific discipline’s method, and examiners deduct for generic or mismatched material even when general knowledge is correct.

bcom-prg.name: BCom prg
bcom-prg.content: B.Com Programme at Delhi University covers accounting, law, management and economics as a balanced commerce degree rather than a specialised honours. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 programme lists Sem 1 DSCs as Business organisation and management (UPC 2412091101), Business Laws (2412091102) and Financial Accounting (2412091103, 3T+1P), each 4 credits. Sem 2-4 then add Corporate Accounting, Company Law, Business Statistics, Financial Management and Entrepreneurship. Students often lose marks on numerical papers — Financial and Cost Accounting, Business Statistics — where format, ledger balancing and formula application are scored step-wise.

english.name: English
english.content: B.A. (Hons) English at Delhi University reads literature chronologically while building critical method. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 programme lists Sem 1 DSCs as Introduction to Literary Studies (UPC 2032101101), European Classical Literature (2032101102) and Indian Classical Literature (2032101103), each 4 credits (3 theory + 1 tutorial). Sem 2-4 continue with 14th-17th Century Poetry, 16th-17th Century Drama, 18th Century Literature, Romantic and Victorian Literature, and American and Indian Writing. Students often lose marks not for lack of reading but for unstructured answers: examiners expect close reading, textual references and a clear argument rather than plot summary.

hindi.name: Hindi
hindi.content: B.A. (Hons) Hindi at Delhi University balances kavya, katha, natak and bhasha-vigyan from Aadikal to contemporary. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 programme lists Sem 1 DSCs as हिंदी कविता : आदिकाल एवं निर्गुण भक्तिकाव्य (UPC 2052101101), हिंदी साहित्य का इतिहास (आदिकाल एवं मध्यकाल) (2052101102) and हिंदी कहानी (2052101103), each 4 credits (3 theory + 1 tutorial). Hindi Sahitya ka Itihas (Aadhunik Kal) and Hindi Nibandh follow in Sem 2, and later Bharatiya Sahitya, Hindi Natak and Samanya Bhasha Vigyan. Students often lose marks when they write general appreciation without textual reference, correct sandarbh and prescribed author-work links that DU expects for each kavya/kahani.

mathematics.name: Mathematics
mathematics.content: B.Sc. (Hons) Mathematics at Delhi University is proof- and problem-driven from the first semester. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 programme lists Sem 1 DSCs as Algebra (UPC 2352011101, 3T+1T), Elementary Real Analysis (2352011102, 3T+1T) and Probability and Statistics (2352011103, 3T+1P). Later semesters build through Linear Algebra, Calculus, Group Theory, Riemann Integration, Multivariate Calculus and Complex Analysis. Students often lose marks by skipping rigorous steps, notation and justification that examiners score in proofs and by leaving numerical work incomplete.

sociology.name: Sociology
sociology.content: B.A. (Hons) Sociology at Delhi University combines classical theory, Indian society and research methods. As of 2026, the UGCF 2022 programme lists Sem 1 DSCs as Introduction to Sociology (UPC 2302101101), Sociology of India I (2302101102) and Introduction to Sociological Research (2302101103), each 4 credits (3 theory + 1 tutorial). Sem 2-4 then cover Sociological Perspectives, Social Stratification, Sociology of India II, Political Sociology and Sociological Thinkers I. Students often lose marks when they describe thinkers or concepts without linking them to Indian examples, contemporary data or the specific question’s directive word (discuss, analyse, critique).

The practical requires reflections and group discussions, a workshop on awareness, and a survey of minimum 25 respondents on duties awareness (p.7). Examination is 'Subject to directions from the Examination Branch' (p.7). The syllabus stresses extension activities and inclusive community work as the practical lens, not just definitions (p.9). Examination is 'Subject to directions from the Examination Branch' with no printed 50/50 table in this PDF. Ramanujan 'A Flowering Tree' and Mamang Dai 'Small Towns and the River'; and Unit III Empathetic exploration and imaginative re-enactments (5 weeks) with Amitav Ghosh Part I Stories from The Great Derangement and two Thangjam Ibopishak poems from Dancing Earth, plus a 15-week practical (pp.35-36). The practical requires field visits to a school/slum/play area to narrate stories, creative re-enactment as play, and a tree plantation drive with adoption of a sapling (p.36). Examination is 'Subject to directions from the Examination Branch'. Students often lose marks by summarising poems without the ecocritical lens (carbon footprint, habitat loss) and by skipping the practical field work viva expects (as of 12 Sept 2026).

The practical lists techniques like mindfulness, conditioned relaxation, boundary setting, empathy display and conflict resolution, with project report option (p.15). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'.
