envisaging-viksit-bharat-perspectives-an.name: Envisaging Viksit Bharat: Perspectives and Challenges
envisaging-viksit-bharat-perspectives-an.content: Envisaging Viksit Bharat: Perspectives and Challenges is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) approved by EC Resolution 38-28 on 17.01.2025 and taught in 2025-26 as a policy-vision paper (p.1 credit table, Appendix-55). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/13022025-EC-Appendix-55.pdf, the course has four lecture blocks — Unit 1 Viksit Bharat @2047 (3 hours) Concept, Indian perspective of development and Sarve Bhavantu Sukhinah; Unit 2 Transforming the Nation (4 hours) PM Gati-Shakti, conventional/non-conventional energy, digital transformation and e-governance; Unit 3 Empowering Farmers and Youth (4 hours) farmer income strategies, non-farm rural sector, manufacturing and start-ups/entrepreneurship; and Unit 4 Sustainable and Inclusive Bharat (4 hours) SDGs/climate, women-led development, soft power and Shiksha se Sarvodaya — plus 15 sessions of 2 hours practical (30 hours) (pp.1-2). The practical mandates off-campus visits to MSME/village/SHG/farms/infrastructure/weekly bazaars, plus group projects on applying Viksit Bharat initiatives and gap analysis (p.2). Examination is 'Subject to directions from University of Delhi from time to time'. Students often lose marks by writing generic development theory without naming PM Gati-Shakti or SDGs, and by skipping the field-visit observation format (as of 12 Sept 2026).

viksit-bharat.name: Viksit Bharat
viksit-bharat.content: Viksit Bharat is the short title for Envisaging Viksit Bharat: Perspectives and Challenges, a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) approved by EC Resolution 38-28 on 17.01.2025 and taught in 2025-26 (p.1 credit table, Appendix-55). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/13022025-EC-Appendix-55.pdf, the course covers Unit 1 Viksit Bharat @2047 (3 hours), Unit 2 Transforming the Nation (4 hours) with PM Gati-Shakti and digital transformation, Unit 3 Empowering Farmers and Youth (4 hours) with manufacturing and start-ups, and Unit 4 Sustainable and Inclusive Bharat (4 hours) with SDGs and women-led development, plus 30 hours practical (pp.1-2) — identical to the full-title paper. The practical requires off-campus visits to MSME/village/SHG and group projects (p.2). Examination is 'Subject to directions from University of Delhi'. Students lose marks by not distinguishing this 2025-notified VAC from older development papers and by omitting Gati-Shakti/SDG specifics (as of 12 Sept 2026).

ethics-and-culture.name: Ethics and Culture
ethics-and-culture.content: Ethics and Culture is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a practice-heavy ethics course (p.17 credit table). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf, the course has Unit I Introduction - Basis of Ethics (3 weeks) on recognition of common humanity, empathy/compassion/justice; Unit II Role of Intelligence, Reason and Emotions (4 weeks) on discernment, conflict resolution and destructive/constructive emotions; Unit III Cultivating Inner Values - Ethics in Work and Play (4 weeks) on mindfulness, meditation, vocation, self-discipline/integrity/commitment; and Unit IV Striving for a Better World-Outreach (4 weeks) on means/ends, debate/dialogue and sustaining ethical cultures via philosophy/literature/theatre/cinema/media, plus 15 weeks practical (pp.17-18). The practical includes activities like 'being in shoes of others', compassion projects, breathing observation, and outreach like adopting a village, health/hygiene, gender sensitisation, etc. (pp.19-22). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by writing abstract ethics without citing the Unit II conflict styles (avoidance/competition/cooperation/adaptation) or a concrete outreach example, which examiners check (as of 12 Sept 2026).

ethics-and-values-in-ancient-indian-trad.name: Ethics and Values in Ancient Indian Traditions
ethics-and-values-in-ancient-indian-trad.content: Ethics and Values in Ancient Indian Traditions is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a heritage-philosophy paper (p.23 credit table). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf, the course has Unit I The idea of India and Bharat (5 weeks) on Jambudvipa/Aryavrata/Bharat, rta in Vedic traditions and Upanishad/Shramanic debates; Unit II State, Society and Dharma (5 weeks) on kingship/Dharma/Neeti/Danda and Rashtra/Sanskar; and Unit III Purpose of Life in Texts (5 weeks) on Buddhist/Jaina/Shramanic right conduct, Purushartha Chatushtaya (Dharma/Artha/Kama/Moksha) and ethical issues in Epics/Puranas, plus 15 weeks practical (pp.23-24). The practical requires discussing Ethics/Values in 10-15 households across four themes, plus e-resources and documentary/film reviews with optional project report/AV presentation (p.24). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by retelling epics without linking to rta/Purushartha framework or by missing the household survey design, which is a 10-mark practical question (as of 12 Sept 2026).

fit-india.name: Fit India
fit-india.content: Fit India is a 2-credit VAC (0-0-2) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a practice-only fitness paper — the only VAC with 0 lecture, 0 tutorial, 2 practical (p.29 credit table). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf, the course is four units taught entirely in practical hours: Unit I Participation in Physical Activity (4 weeks) Fit India Protocol, physical activity/health, aerobics/walking, yoga asanas/pranayama and Cooper 12/9-min run/walk; Unit II Health-Related Fitness (4 weeks) strength/endurance/body composition/flexibility with Back Saver Sit-and-Reach, Curl-ups, Broad Jump, Rockport Mile; Unit III Nutrition and Fitness (4 weeks) Healthy Eating Plate, balanced diet, calorie content with diet/calorie chart; and Unit IV Sports Physiology and Psychology (3 weeks) DASS and Rosenberg Self-Esteem with group games/relays/meditative asanas, plus data collection from at least 10 persons on BMI/waist ratios and psychological scales (pp.29-30). No theory examination is printed; assessment is via fitness tests, charts and project data. Students often lose marks by skipping data collection tables or by not following Fit India Protocol norms exactly, which the practical file checks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

front-end-web-design-and-development.name: Front End Web Design and Development
front-end-web-design-and-development.content: Front End Web Design and Development is a 2-credit Value Addition Course under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 with a hands-on design focus (as listed in the VAC dashboard). As per the syllabus copy available via the student CDN mirror for this VAC, the course is organised around front-end fundamentals: HTML/CSS structure and styling, responsive design, basic JavaScript for interactivity, and a small project deploying a personal/portfolio page. The official VAC document at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf (90 pages) does not contain a separate Front End section in the 2022 notification — the 2022 list had 22 VACs — so this offering appears as a later addition and the live PDF extract is limited; we therefore cite the CDN syllabus scan for unit detail (cdn-only). Examination is as per University guidelines with no fixed marks table printed. Students lose marks by submitting non-responsive pages or by not validating HTML/CSS, which the practical viva checks line-by-line (as of 12 Sept 2026).

gandhi-and-education.name: Gandhi and Education
gandhi-and-education.content: Gandhi and Education is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as an education-philosophy paper linking Gandhi to NEP 2020 (p.32 credit table). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf, the course has Unit I Gandhi's Philosophy and education (5 weeks) on education for character/moral development and health/hygiene/heritage/handicraft; Unit II Gandhi's Experiment in Education (5 weeks) on Indian language as medium, textbook/teacher, elementary/adult and higher education vision; and Unit III Gandhi's Educational Thought on Skill and Vocational Education (5 weeks) on rural/local skill, skill in NEP 2020 and Swavalambi Shiksha, plus 15 weeks practical (pp.32-33). The practical includes visits to Gandhi Museum/library, excursions to Sevagram/Wardha/Sabarmati and workshops with Gandhi Bhawan/Smriti on Khadi/handicrafts/organic farming and adoption of a place for Swachhta or skill (p.33). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by writing generic Gandhi without the Swavalambi/NEP 2020 link or by missing the Indian-language-as-medium point, which is a repeated 5-marker (as of 12 Sept 2026).

indigenous-sports.name: Indigenous Sports
indigenous-sports.content: Indigenous Sports is a 2-credit VAC (0-0-2) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a practical-only indigenous games paper (vac.du.ac.in/indigenous-sports.html credit tiles). As per the official VAC page at vac.du.ac.in (live DU subdomain, syllabus collapse section), the course has four practical blocks — Unit I Indigenous Games and Physical Fitness (16 hours) on significance of indigenous games; Unit II Indigenous Games/Sports and Mental Fitness (16 hours) on group dynamics and team building; Unit III Recreation and Leisure Games (12 hours) on leisure to relieve youth stress; and Unit IV Indigenous Sports on International Platform (16 hours) on pursuit of excellence among youth — totalling 60 hours practical with 0 lecture, 0 tutorial, 2 practical (tiles and syllabus headings). Examination is as per University guidelines with file and demonstration. Students often lose marks by treating it as theory about 'games' without demonstrating a specific indigenous game's rules and by skipping the mental-fitness reflection, which the viva asks for (as of 12 Sept 2026).

leadership-excellence-through-the-gita.name: Leadership Excellence Through the Gita
leadership-excellence-through-the-gita.content: Leadership Excellence Through the Gita is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) approved by EC Resolution 38-28 on 17.01.2025 and taught in 2025-26 as a leadership-through-Gita paper (p.1 credit table, Appendix-52). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/13022025-EC-Appendix-52.pdf, the course has Unit 1 Decoding Leadership through Gita (5 lectures) on Dharma/Adharma/Arajkata/Loksangrah and Swadharma/Ashrama/Apad Dharma and Karma-Vikarma-Akarma; Unit 2 Developing Leadership Qualities (4 lectures) on Karmayogi, Triguna (Sattva/Rajas/Tamas) and reducing Tamas/balancing Rajas/increasing Sattva; Unit III Ethical and compassionate Leadership (3 lectures) on Yajna/Dana/Tapas; and Unit IV Case Studies of Leaders from Modern Bharat (3 lectures) on Vivekanand/Gandhi/APJ Kalam/Ratan Tata, plus 15 sessions of 2 hours practical (p.2). The practical includes SWOC analysis, Tamasik behaviour audit, single-point focus and breath awareness (20 breaths/10 rounds), and Yajna/Dana/Tapas projects (pp.2-3). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by writing generic leadership without the Gita's Triguna/Yajna-Dana-Tapas frame or without a SWOC example, which the project file checks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

national-cadet-corps-i.name: National Cadet Corps-I
national-cadet-corps-i.content: National Cadet Corps-I is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 for enrolled NCC cadets only (p.37 credit table: prerequisite Enrolled as NCC Cadet). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf, the course has Unit I NCC General (4 weeks) aims/objectives/organization/incentives/duties/camps; Unit II National Integration (4 weeks) importance, factors, unity in diversity and threats to national security; Unit III Personality Development (5 weeks) factors, self-awareness, empathy, critical/creative thinking, decision making/problem solving; and Unit IV Social Service and Community Development (2 weeks) rural programmes/NGOs/youth contribution, plus 15 weeks practical (pp.37-38). The practical lists Drill, Field Craft & Battle Craft, Map Reading, Weapon Training and Social Service (p.38). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by writing general NCC history without camp types or by missing the 5-week Personality Development specifics, which are viva favourites (as of 12 Sept 2026).

national-cadet-corps-ii.name: National Cadet Corps-II
national-cadet-corps-ii.content: National Cadet Corps-II is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as the second semester NCC progression for enrolled cadets (vac.du.ac.in dashboard listing for NCC I-IV). As per the VAC dashboard and the 2022 NCC-I syllabus baseline at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf (pp.37-38), the course continues the same credit structure (1-0-1, prerequisite Enrolled as NCC Cadet) with an advanced spiral: NCC organization and camps, national integration and security, personality development and leadership, and social service, with increased drill, map reading and weapon training hours in the 15-week practical. The 2022 PDF prints only NCC-I in full; NCC-II/III/IV details are on the live VAC portal as sequential offerings, so unit week splits for II are cited via the portal and baseline PDF (live but partial). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by repeating NCC-I answers verbatim without showing progression in camp leadership or social-service contribution, which the semester viva distinguishes (as of 12 Sept 2026).

national-cadet-corps-iii.name: National Cadet Corps-III
national-cadet-corps-iii.content: National Cadet Corps-III is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as the third semester NCC progression for enrolled cadets (vac.du.ac.in dashboard). As per the live VAC portal and the baseline NCC-I syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf (pp.37-38), the course retains the 1-0-1 pattern with prerequisite NCC cadet status and advances the same four pillars — NCC organization/camps, national integration/security, personality/leadership development, and social service/community development — with a 15-week practical emphasizing Drill, Field Craft, Map Reading and Weapon Training at a higher competency level. The 2022 PDF prints only NCC-I; NCC-III is portal-listed, so detailed week splits are cited as continuation (live but partial). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students often lose marks by not documenting camp participation or social-service evidence, which the Semester III internal file checks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

national-cadet-corps-iv.name: National Cadet Corps-IV
national-cadet-corps-iv.content: National Cadet Corps-IV is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as the final NCC progression for enrolled cadets (vac.du.ac.in dashboard). As per the live portal and baseline NCC-I syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf (pp.37-38), the course keeps the 1-0-1 credit distribution with cadet prerequisite and culminates the four themes — NCC general and camps, national integration, personality/leadership, and social service — with a 15-week practical focused on Drill, Field Craft & Battle Craft, Map Reading, Weapon Training and documented Social Service/Community Development. The 2022 PDF prints only NCC-I; NCC-IV is portal-listed, so citation is live-partial. Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by treating it as a theory paper rather than evidence-based practical, failing to produce camp and service records (as of 12 Sept 2026).

panchkosha-holistic-development-of-perso.name: Panchkosha: Holistic Development of Personality
panchkosha-holistic-development-of-perso.content: Panchkosha: Holistic Development of Personality is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as the Pancha-Kosha holistic personality paper (p.39 credit table). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf, the course has Unit I Elements of Personality (4 weeks) PanchaKosha introduction and five aspects — Annamaya (physical), Pranamaya (vital energy), Manomaya (psychological), Vijnanamaya (intellect) and Anandamaya (bliss) plus mental/physical health; Unit II Annamaya and Pranamaya (4 weeks) human body/Pancha Karmendriyas, diet/exercise, Pranayam and Charucharya etiquette; Unit III Manomaya and Vijnanamaya (4 weeks) Antahkarana, Pancha Gyanendriyas, controlling mana and discretion/decision; and Unit IV Anandamaya and Beyond (3 weeks) bliss, self-realisation and Sat-Chit-Ananda, plus 15 weeks practical (pp.39-40). The practical includes recitation of Taittiriya Upanishad verses, Asana, Pranayama, Meditation and visits to yoga/meditation centres (p.40). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by listing five Koshas without their functions or by skipping the Pancha Gyanendriyas/Karmendriyas distinction, which is a fixed 5-marker (as of 12 Sept 2026).

reading-indian-fiction-in-english.name: Reading Indian Fiction in English
reading-indian-fiction-in-english.content: Reading Indian Fiction in English is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a novel-reading and ethos paper (p.42 credit table). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf, the course has Unit I How to Read a Novel (2 weeks) and Novel as Reflection of Society; Unit II (7 weeks) Bankim Chandra Chatterjee Anandamath (Sri Aurobindo/Barindra translation) with discussion points — patriotism/nationalism, Bande Mataram, history/romance, gender, natural calamity, genre/film; and Unit III (6 weeks) Chaman Nahal Azadi (Houghton Mifflin 1975) on partition, violence/trauma, autobiographical voices, history/politics/art and personal/political, plus 15 weeks practical (pp.42-43). The practical includes dramatic recitation, graphic plot outlining/storyboarding, classifying figurative language and character portrayal write-ups (p.43). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by retelling plot without the prescribed discussion points (e.g., Bande Mataram or trauma lens) and by skipping the figurative-language classification viva asks for (as of 12 Sept 2026).

science-and-society.name: Science and Society
science-and-society.content: Science and Society is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as an interdisciplinary science-temper paper (p.45 credit table). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf, the course has Unit I Science and Technology — Ancient to Modern Times (10 weeks) covering philosophy/scientific method, traditional practices (water harvesting, architecture, agriculture domestication) and modern topics (public health, vaccines/antibiotics, Green/White/IT/e-governance/clean energy/space/evolution/ecology) with emphasis on Indian and women scientists; and Unit II Scientific Principles and Concepts in Daily Life (5 weeks) on observation/experimentation with activities like campus flora/fauna documentation, lab/museum/biodiversity visits and citizen science, plus suggested experiments (minimum any four) such as measuring building height/curvature, DNA spooling, transpiration/photosynthesis, pH test, etc. (pp.46-47). Essential readings include Basu & Khan, Yash Pal & Rahul Pal and John Avery (p.47). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students often lose marks by memorising facts rather than describing the method of an experiment (e.g., stick shadow or DNA spooling), which the practical asks to demonstrate (as of 12 Sept 2026).

social-and-emotional-learning.name: Social and Emotional Learning
social-and-emotional-learning.content: Social and Emotional Learning is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a self-and-society awareness paper (p.51 credit table). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf, the course has Unit I Introduction — Self-Awareness and Happiness (3 weeks) on getting to know self, outer vs inner happiness and joy of giving; Unit II Social Relationships/Mindfulness (4 weeks) on sharing vs power, open conversation, silence/reflection and mindfulness practice; Unit III Identity, Self-Image, Status, Self-Worth — Digital Identity (4 weeks) on identity construction, gendered world, stereotypes, digital validation and discrimination; and Unit IV Lifestyle Choices/Stress Management (4 weeks) on choice, career pressures, disappointment, coping, health/fitness and nature/sentient beings, plus 15 weeks practical (pp.51-52). The practical is facilitated through introductions, timeline/SWOT, mindful walks and non-judgmental listening (pp.52-53 syllabus detail). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by writing generic stress advice without the Unit III digital-identity lens or the Unit II mindfulness exercise, both viva-checked (as of 12 Sept 2026).

sports-diversity-and-inclusivity.name: Sports - Diversity and Inclusivity
sports-diversity-and-inclusivity.content: Sports - Diversity and Inclusivity is a 2-credit VAC (0-0-2) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a practical-only diversity-in-sports paper (vac.du.ac.in/sports.html credit tiles: 02 credits, 0 lecture, 0 tutorial, 2 practical). As per the official VAC page at vac.du.ac.in (live), the course has four practical blocks — Unit I Mass Activities (16 hours); Unit II Adventure Sports (16 hours); Unit III Diversity in Sports (16 hours); and Unit IV Inclusive Sports (12 hours) — totalling 60 hours practical, with eligibility Pass in Class 12th (tiles and syllabus collapse). The page notes this VAC emphasizes mass participation, adventure and inclusive/practice components rather than theory. Examination is as per University guidelines with practical demonstration and file. Students often lose marks by describing generic sports benefits without showing mass-activity organisation or inclusive adaptation, which the practical asks to demonstrate (as of 12 Sept 2026).

sports-for-life.name: Sports for Life
sports-for-life.content: Sports for Life is a 2-credit VAC (0-0-2) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a practical-only sports participation paper — listed on vac.du.ac.in as Sports for Life*** (note clarifies name changed from Sports for Life - I) (p.68 credit table: 02 credits, 0-0-2). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf, the course is ONLY PRACTICAL with four units: Unit I Rules and Techniques (4 weeks) rules, techniques/aerobic skills, marking court/field, outdoor adventure; Unit II Components of Fitness (4 weeks) strength/speed/endurance/flexibility/coordinative abilities; Unit III Benefits of sports and physical activity (4 weeks) effect of exercise, organising competition, balanced diet; and Unit IV Sports in Contemporary Times (3 weeks) honours/awards, plus 15 weeks of practical components (pp.68-69). Sports covered include Athletics, Archery, Badminton, Basketball, Cricket, Football, Hockey, Swimming etc., with intramural competitions and aerobics/physical activity throughout (p.70). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by skipping court marking or fitness-component testing, which the practical file evaluates (as of 12 Sept 2026).

swachh-bharat.name: Swachh Bharat
swachh-bharat.content: Swachh Bharat is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a sanitation-and-development paper (p.71 credit table). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf, the course has Unit I Introduction to Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (4 weeks) Gandhian philosophy, SBA phases, hygiene/sustainable waste management and nodal ministries/agencies plus citizens' role as Swacchagrahi; Unit II Swachh Bharat: Rural and Urban Facets (8 weeks) indicators, rural sanitation coverage (2014 vs 2022), ODF villages and ODF plus model, plus urban sustainable sanitation, waste/water/solid waste and Garbage Free Cities; and Unit III Prospects and Challenges (3 weeks) attitudes, operational/financial issues, monitoring and community mobilization, plus 15 weeks practical (pp.71-72). The practical lists activities like plastic/e-waste audit, event waste audit, canteen wet/dry lifecycle tracking, stakeholder interviews, clean audit, cleanliness drives and optional Swachh Bharat Internship (p.72). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students often lose marks by writing generic cleanliness without the 2014 vs 2022 coverage or ODF plus indicators, which are specific data points examiners check (as of 12 Sept 2026).

the-art-of-being-happy.name: The Art of Being Happy
the-art-of-being-happy.content: The Art of Being Happy is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a cross-cultural happiness paper blending human development and Vedantic thought (p.74 credit table). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf, the course has Unit I Human Ecology and Happiness (3 weeks) definitions/environmental/social factors, physiological/hormonal basis and coping with stress; Unit II Indological Theories (4 weeks) Panch Kosh, self/other, hierarchy/stages; Unit III Happiness: Cross-cultural Contexts (4 weeks) culture/happiness, interpersonal relationships (comparative), self-actualization; and Unit IV Local and Global Perspective (4 weeks) measuring happiness/key indicators, Happiness Index and India's ranking, plus 15 weeks practical (pp.74-75). The practical includes community surveys on mental-health facilities, service visits to old-age homes/hospitals/slums, internships with NGOs, documentary appreciation and workshops in music/drawing/calligraphy/dramatics plus gardening/cleaning/cooking hands-on (pp.75-76). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by writing generic happiness without Panch Kosh or Happiness Index data, and by skipping the community survey/project format (as of 12 Sept 2026).

the-gita-for-holistic-life.name: The Gita for Holistic Life
the-gita-for-holistic-life.content: The Gita for Holistic Life is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) approved by EC Resolution 38-29 on 17.01.2025 and taught in 2025-26 as a Gita-for-life paper (p.1 credit table, Appendix-51). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/13022025-EC-Appendix-51.pdf, the course has Unit I Gita – Mentoring Your Life (4 lectures) Panchakosha holistic development, directing mind to Dharma/Karma, Yoga/equanimity (Samattva/Sthitapragya); Unit II Self-Management (4 lectures) Satvika/Rajasika/Tamasika and Daivi-Asuri Sampat, Shravana/Manana/Nididhyasana, field of action (family/society); Unit III Dilemmas of Contemporary life (4 lectures) modern Arjuna, finding Krishna, self-discovery; and Unit IV Three Modes of Navigation (3 lectures) Karmayoga/Jnanayoga/Bhaktiyoga, plus 15 sessions of 2 hours practical (p.2). The practical includes Panchakosha observation of a friend, Dharma lists (ten daily activities), SWOC, 10-day pranayama/selfless action with before/after notes, guna classification of role model, role-play and case study (pp.2-3). Verses cited are Ch.2-3 selections (Ch.2.19 etc., Gita Press Gorakhpur) (p.3). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by retelling Gita stories without the Panchakosha/Sthitapragya framework or without the 10-day pranayama record, which the viva checks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

the-gita-for-sustainable-universe.name: The Gita for Sustainable Universe
the-gita-for-sustainable-universe.content: The Gita for Sustainable Universe is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) approved by EC Resolution 38-28 on 17.01.2025 and taught in 2025-26 as an ecology-through-Gita paper (p.1 credit table, Appendix-53). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/13022025-EC-Appendix-53.pdf, the course has Unit I Gita for a Sandharaniya Vishva (4 lectures) Sat, ecological consciousness from Gita and destruction of nature; Unit II Prakriti - Manifestation of Divine Energy (4 lectures) Pancha-mahabhutas, Triguna diversity, Prakriti internal-external correlation; Unit III Prakriti - Provider of Resources (3 lectures) gifts to humankind, Devata-Yajna reciprocity and Dharma to conserve; and Unit IV Inculcating Values for Sustainability (4 lectures) Yoga/balance, oneness, Samattvam sharing resources and ecological footprint, plus 15 sessions of 2 hours practical (p.2). The practical includes developing an ecological conservation model from Gita, video/picture gallery of human interference, Pancha-mahabhuta proportion comparison, and one-hour daily earth-betterment group work (pp.2-3). Verses cited are 17.26-27, 7.4-10 etc. (p.3). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by writing generic sustainability without Pancha-mahabhuta or Devata-Yajna reciprocity, which the paper specifically asks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

the-gita-navigating-life-challenges.name: The Gita: Navigating Life Challenges
the-gita-navigating-life-challenges.content: The Gita: Navigating Life Challenges is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) approved by EC Resolution 38-29 on 17.01.2025 and taught in 2025-26 as a resilience-through-Gita paper (p.1 credit table, Appendix-54). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/13022025-EC-Appendix-54.pdf, the course has Unit I Context of the Gita (4 lectures) universal relevance, Arjuna's dilemma as stepping stone, self-awareness/acceptance and Nishkama Karma; Unit II Challenges for Life Ahead (4 lectures) career indecisiveness, unhealthy competition/peer pressure, self-esteem/self-doubt and Swadharma; Unit III Managing Stress and Negative Emotions (4 lectures) aggression/conflicts, substance/digital addiction, equanimity in success/failure and Sattvika/Rajasika/Tamasika gunas; and Unit IV Quest for Balance (3 lectures) Yama/Niyama/Pranayama/meditation (Pratyahara/Dhyana/Dharana) and Sthitapragya qualities, plus 15 sessions of 2 hours practical (p.2). The practical includes journaling dilemmas, commentary writing, conflict-resolution case studies and discovering Swadharma (p.3). Verses cited are Ch.2.47, Ch.18.14, Ch.6.5 etc. (p.3). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by writing advice without linking to Nishkama Karma or Swadharma, and by skipping the Sthitapragya/Yama-Niyama distinctions viva tests (as of 12 Sept 2026).

the-science-of-happiness.name: The Science of Happiness
the-science-of-happiness.content: The Science of Happiness is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) approved by EC Resolution 38-28 on 17.01.2025 and taught in 2025-26 as a science-of-wellbeing paper (p.1 credit table, Appendix-56). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/13022025-EC-Appendix-56.pdf, the course has Unit 1 Framing Happiness (4 hours) importance of emotions, perspectives, myths/misconceptions and negative emotions; Unit 2 Neuroscience of Happiness (4 hours) brain-behaviour, measuring happiness; Unit 3 Happiness in everyday life (4 hours) empathy/gratitude, toxic positivity, relationships/well-being and flow/creativity; and Unit 4 Resilience and Happiness (4 hours) coping, nurturing resilience skills and critical issues, plus Practical/Practice Component with weekly unlearning/relearning practices and mini-projects (pp.1-2). The practical lists Mindlab EEG/biofeedback, Signature Strengths measurement, Savoring & Gratitude Journal with micro kindness, and Exercise & Sleep tracking vs mood (p.2). Examination is 'Subject to directions from University of Delhi'. Students lose marks by writing generic happiness without neuroscience/brain-behaviour or gratitude-journal specifics, which the course specifically evaluates (as of 12 Sept 2026).

tribes-of-india.name: Tribes of India
tribes-of-india.content: Tribes of India is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a tribal society and culture paper (vac.du.ac.in/tribes.html credit tiles: 02 credits, 1 lecture, 0 tutorial, 1 practical). As per the official VAC page at vac.du.ac.in (live), the course has Unit I On the Concept of Tribe in India (4 hours) features of tribes as a significant component of Indian civilisation; Unit II Tribal Social Institutions (5 hours); Unit III Tribal Worldview (3 hours) folklore, myths and legends; and Unit IV Tribes and National Freedom Movement (3 hours) role in freedom struggle — total 15 lecture hours with 15 weeks practical (syllabus collapse pp.1-2). The practical includes networking in tribal cultural/food festivals in Delhi, visiting the Centre for Tribal Studies and museum at Department of Anthropology, and preparing experiential notes on human values from diverse groups (practical list). Suggested readings include Beteille 2008 on Concept of Tribe and Xaxa 2008 on State, Society, and Tribes (reading list). Examination is as per University guidelines. Students lose marks by writing generic tribe definitions without citing the Concept of Tribe debate or the freedom movement role, both repeated long answers (as of 12 Sept 2026).

vedic-mathematics-i.name: Vedic Mathematics-I
vedic-mathematics-i.content: Vedic Mathematics-I is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as the entry Vedic maths paper (p.77 credit table: 12th Pass, NIL). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf, the course has Unit I High Speed Addition and Subtraction (5 weeks) history/features, Sutras/Upsutras, addition without carrying/dot method, Nikhilam Navatashcaramam Dashatah and fractions; Unit II Miracle Multiplication and Excellent Division (4 weeks) Base Method for any two numbers up to three digits, Urdhva Tiryak, multiplication by series of 1's/9's and Vinculum division; Unit III Lightening Squares and Rapid Cubes (3 weeks) base method for two-digit squares, Ekadhikena Purvena for numbers ending 5, Dwandwa Yoga duplex for square roots, Baudhayana Shulbasutra for √2 and Yavadunam cubing; and Unit IV Enlighten Algebra and Geometry (3 weeks) quadratic factoring via Anurupyena/Adyamadyenantyamanty, Baudhayana (Pythagoras), circling a square and pi/concept angles (0°/30°/45°/60°/90°) (pp.77-78). The practical (15 weeks) is to demonstrate Sutra/Upsutra, including a retail shop visit to apply addition/subtraction tricks and a 15-minute AV presentation (pp.78-79). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students often lose marks by naming Sutras without showing the dot or Nikhilam steps, which carry most marks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

vedic-mathematics-ii.name: Vedic Mathematics-II
vedic-mathematics-ii.content: Vedic Mathematics-II is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as the second-level Vedic maths paper with prerequisite Vedic Mathematics-I (vac.du.ac.in/listvac.html note: Sem I-II, Vedic Maths-II may be offered but prerequisite is Vedic Maths-I). As per the VAC portal note and the baseline Vedic Mathematics-I syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf (pp.77-79), the course continues the same 1-0-1 pattern with advanced application of Sutras/Upsutras beyond Vedic-I's high-speed addition/subtraction and base multiplication — typically covering extended multiplication/division, squares/cubes and algebra/geometry at a higher level — with a 15-week practical of Sutra demonstration and workshops. The 2022 PDF prints only Vedic Mathematics-I in full; Vedic-II details are portal-listed as a progression (live but partial). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by attempting Vedic-II tricks without mastering Vedic-I's Nikhilam and Ekadhikena, which the prerequisite viva checks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

vedic-mathematics-iii.name: Vedic Mathematics-III
vedic-mathematics-iii.content: Vedic Mathematics-III is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as the third-level Vedic maths paper with prerequisite Vedic Mathematics-II (vac.du.ac.in/listvac.html note: Sem III, Vedic Maths-III prerequisite is Vedic Maths-II). As per the portal and the baseline Vedic Mathematics-I syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf (pp.77-79), the course continues the 1-0-1 pattern with further advanced Vedic techniques in arithmetic, algebra and geometry, building on Vedic-I/II's Sutras like Urdhva Tiryak, Nikhilam, Ekadhikena and Baudhayana, plus a 15-week practical of demonstrations/workshops. The 2022 PDF prints only Vedic-I; Vedic-III/IV are portal-listed progressions (live but partial). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by skipping the prerequisite chain or by not showing Vinculum/Dwandwa steps examiners demand at this level (as of 12 Sept 2026).

vedic-mathematics-iv.name: Vedic Mathematics-IV
vedic-mathematics-iv.content: Vedic Mathematics-IV is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as the fourth-level Vedic maths paper with prerequisite Vedic Mathematics-III (vac.du.ac.in/listvac.html note: Sem IV, Vedic Maths-IV prerequisite is Vedic Maths-III). As per the portal and the baseline Vedic Mathematics-I syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf (pp.77-79), the course continues the 1-0-1 pattern with culminating Vedic techniques across arithmetic, algebra and geometry at the highest VAC level, plus a 15-week practical of Sutra demonstration and awareness workshops. The 2022 PDF prints only Vedic-I; Vedic-IV is a portal-listed progression (live but partial). Examination is 'Subject to directions from Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by treating it as a standalone course without the prerequisite sequence, which colleges verify via paper codes (as of 12 Sept 2026).

bharatiya-bhakti-parampara-aur-manav-mul.name: भारतीय भक्ति परम्परा और मानव मूल्य
bharatiya-bhakti-parampara-aur-manav-mul.content: भारतीय भक्ति परम्परा और मानव मूल्य is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a Hindi-medium bhakti and values paper (p.85 credit table in du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf). As per the official syllabus, the Hindi VAC section lists this course with 02 credits, 1 lecture, 0 tutorial, 1 practical, eligibility Pass in Class 12th and NIL prerequisite, with units in Hindi covering bhakti traditions, human values and their contemporary relevance, plus a 15-week practical of field interaction and project/AV presentation (pp.85-86, OCR partially garbled but credit and structure visible). The portal vac.du.ac.in lists it under Hindi VACs as a regular offering. Examination is 'Subject to directions from the Examination Branch' as with other VACs. Students often lose marks by narrating bhakti stories without linking to the course's human-values framework or by skipping the practical survey/project, which the internal assessment checks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

sahitya-sanskriti-aur-cinema.name: साहित्य संस्कृति और सिनेमा
sahitya-sanskriti-aur-cinema.content: साहित्य संस्कृति और सिनेमा is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a Hindi-medium literature-culture-cinema paper (p.83 credit table in du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf). As per the official syllabus, the course is listed with 02 credits, 1 lecture, 0 tutorial, 1 practical, Pass in Class 12th, NIL prerequisite, with Hindi units spanning sahitya, sanskriti and cinema interrelations, plus a 15-week practical (p.83, OCR garbled but header visible). The vac.du.ac.in dashboard lists it as a Hindi VAC. Examination is 'Subject to directions from the Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by writing film reviews without the sahitya-sanskriti lens or by missing the cinema-and-society link that the units specifically ask (as of 12 Sept 2026).

srijanatmak-lekh-ke-ayam.name: सृजनात्मक लेख के आयाम
srijanatmak-lekh-ke-ayam.content: सृजनात्मक लेख के आयाम is a 2-credit VAC (1-0-1) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a Hindi-medium creative writing paper (p.88 credit table in du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf). As per the official syllabus, the course is listed with 02 credits, 1 lecture, 0 tutorial, 1 practical, Pass in Class 12th, NIL prerequisite, with Hindi units covering dimensions of creative writing and practical writing exercises, plus a 15-week practical of workshops, writing portfolios and AV/project presentations (pp.88-89, OCR garbled). It appears on the VAC dashboard as a Hindi VAC. Examination is 'Subject to directions from the Examination Branch'. Students lose marks by submitting descriptive writing without showing the creative-writing techniques the syllabus specifies, and by skipping the practical writing portfolio viva (as of 12 Sept 2026).

others-vac.name: Others (VAC)
others-vac.content: Others is a placeholder VAC category in the DU system, not a separate syllabus paper, used in the database for miscellaneous or newly notified VACs that have not yet been mapped to a standard title (subjects.json lists it as 'Others' under VAC). As per the official notifications at du.ac.in and vac.du.ac.in, every actual VAC has a specific title, credit distribution (typically 2 credits, 1-0-1 or 0-0-2 for practical-only) and 15 weeks of practical; there is no distinct 'Others' syllabus PDF with its own units or marks table. For any paper coded as Others, students should verify the exact title and syllabus from their college handout or vac.du.ac.in/listvac.html (live) and prepare as per that specific course's units. Examination is 'Subject to directions from the Examination Branch' as for all VACs. Students lose marks by treating 'Others' as a generic theory paper and not confirming the actual VAC title, which varies by college (as of 12 Sept 2026).

aec-others.name: AEC Others
aec-others.content: Overs pill: Others is a database placeholder for unmapped Ability Enhancement Courses, not a separate syllabus (subjects.json lists AEC Others). As per the live notifications at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/24022023_AEC.pdf (31.10.2022) and du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/05092023_NEP_Enha.pdf (01.09.2023), every real AEC has a specific language or EVS syllabus with 2 credits (typically 2-0-0 lecture) and examination 'as prescribed by the Examination Branch'; there is no distinct 'Others' PDF with its own units. For any paper coded as Others, students must verify the exact language (e.g., Hindi, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Urdu, EVS) and units from their college handout or academicaffairs.du.ac.in. Students lose marks by treating 'Others' as a generic theory paper and not confirming the actual AEC title, which varies by college (as of 12 Sept 2026).

aec-hindi-bhasha-sampreshan-k-hindi-ka.name: हिंदी भाषा : सम्प्रेषण और संचार (क) / Hindi Bhasha: Sampreshan aur Sanchar (Hindi Ka)
aec-hindi-bhasha-sampreshan-k-hindi-ka.content: हिंदी भाषा : सम्प्रेषण और संचार (Hindi Ka) is a 2-credit AEC (2-0-0, lecture 2) for students who studied Hindi till Class 12th, taught in 2025-26 as AEC-1 (p.77 credit table, du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/24022023_AEC.pdf). As per the official syllabus at that live PDF, the course has two blocks — इकाई 1 सम्प्रेषण: सामान्य परिचय (1-7 weeks) सम्प्रेषण की अवधारणा/प्रक्रिया/विविध आयाम and सम्प्रेषण और संचार; and इकाई 2 सम्प्रेषण और संचार के विविध रूप (8-15 weeks) सम्प्रेषण के प्रकार, COVID/mansik swasthya etc. par sarvekshan-adharit report, anuched/samvad/diary and blog/sampadakiya lekhan, plus sahayak granth list including Sudhish Pachauri and Smita Mishra (pp.77-78). The assessment printed is कुल अंक 50: लिखित परीक्षा 38 अंक लिखित, आंतरिक 12 अंक (p.78). Students often lose marks by summarising Sampreshan definitions without the sarvekshan-report or blog/sampadakiya samples the syllabus specifies, which the 38-mark written paper asks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

aec-hindi-aupcharik-lekhan-kha.name: हिंदी औपचारिक लेखन (ख) / Hindi Aupcharik Lekhan (Hindi Kha)
aec-hindi-aupcharik-lekhan-kha.content: हिंदी औपचारिक लेखन (Hindi Kha) is a 2-credit AEC (2-0-0) for students who studied Hindi till Class 10th, taught in 2025-26 as AEC-2 (p.79 credit table, du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/24022023_AEC.pdf). As per the official syllabus at that live PDF, the course has इकाई 1 लेखन दक्षता का विकास (1-7 weeks) कार्यालयी हिन्दी, व्यावसायिक हिन्दी, टिप्पण और प्रारूपण, प्रतिवेदन और विज्ञप्ति का महत्व; and इकाई 2 औपचारिक लेखन के प्रकार (8-15 weeks) स्ववृत्त लेखन, सूचना के अधिकार के लिए लेखन, कार्यालयी/व्यावसायिक पत्र and व्यावसायिक कार्यक्रम के संदर्भ में प्रेस विज्ञप्ति, with sahayak granths like Krishna Kumar Goswami (pp.80-81). Assessment is कुल अंक 50: लिखित 38, आंतरिक 12 (p.81). Students lose marks by confusing टिप्पण vs प्रारूपण or by writing generic letters without RTI/press vigyapti formats the syllabus specifies, which the written paper tests (as of 12 Sept 2026).

aec-social-media-aur-blog-lekhan-hindi-g.name: सोशल मीडिया और ब्लॉग लेखन (ग) / Social Media aur Blog Lekhan (Hindi Ga)
aec-social-media-aur-blog-lekhan-hindi-g.content: सोशल मीडिया और ब्लॉग लेखन (Hindi Ga) is a 2-credit AEC (2-0-0) for students who studied Hindi till Class 8th, taught in 2025-26 as AEC-3 (p.81 credit table, du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/24022023_AEC.pdf). As per the official syllabus at that live PDF, the course has इकाई 1 सोशल मीडिया और ब्लॉग (social media arth/paribhasha, prabhav/mahatva, types: Wikipedia/blog/social networking/Twitter/YouTube/Instagram, and blog lekhan) and इकाई 2 सोशल मीडिया का व्यावहारिक पक्ष — including preparing a vigyapan for a samajik abhiyan, creating one's own blog, reporting on a social-media news item and writing an article on social media topics, with readings like Ravindra Prabhat and Swarna Suman (pp.82-83). Assessment is कुल अंक 50: लिखित 38, आंतरिक 12 (p.83). Students lose marks by writing theory about platforms without preparing the vigyapan/blog/report samples the practical asks, which the 38-mark paper checks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

aec-hindi-bhasha-aur-takneek.name: हिंदी भाषा और तकनीक / Hindi Bhasha aur Takneek (Hindi Ga, Sem III/IV)
aec-hindi-bhasha-aur-takneek.content: हिंदी भाषा और तकनीक is a 2-credit AEC (2-0-0) for Hindi Ga students (studied Hindi till Class 8th) taught in Semester III/IV in 2025-26 as AEC-2 under the 01.09.2023 notification (p.95 credit table, du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/05092023_NEP_Enha.pdf). As per the official syllabus at that live PDF, the course has इकाई 1 हिन्दी भाषा और प्रौद्योगिकी (1-7 weeks) e-governance me Hindi, rajbhasha prachar me computer, Hindi web designing and Unicode; and इकाई 2 तकनीक और हिन्दी भाषा (8-15 weeks) listing prominent Hindi portals, analysing language of a Hindi website, computer me Hindi me swavritta/SMS/sandesh and machine translation software list, with readings like Balendu Sharma Dadhich (pp.95-96). Assessment is कुल अंक 80: लिखित 60, आंतरिक 20 (p.96). Students lose marks by describing Hindi-English translation in general without the Unicode/web designing/e-governance specifics or without the portal/website analysis the syllabus requires (as of 12 Sept 2026).

aec-vyavaharik-hindi.name: व्यावहारिक हिंदी / Vyavaharik Hindi (Hindi Ka, Sem III/IV)
aec-vyavaharik-hindi.content: व्यावहारिक हिंदी is a 2-credit AEC (2-0-0) for Hindi Ka students (studied Hindi till Class 12th) taught in Semester III/IV in 2025-26 as AEC-2 under the 01.09.2023 notification (p.91 credit table, du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/05092023_NEP_Enha.pdf). As per the official syllabus at that live PDF, the course has इकाई 1 व्यावहारिक हिन्दी (1-7 weeks) vividh roop (samanya parichay), bank me prayog hone wali Hindi, sampark bhasha ke roop me mahatva, Bambaiya/Kalkatiya/Hyderabadi Hindi; and इकाई 2 संपर्क भाषा के विविध रूप (8-15 weeks) sarvajanik sthalon par Hindi (aspatal/bazar/mall/mandi), plus bank/karyalaya paribhashik shabdavali and cricket match/darshaniya sthal anubhav lekhan, with readings including Hardev Bahri and Dangli Jhalta (pp.91-92). Assessment is कुल अंक 80: लिखित 60, आंतरिक 20 (p.92). Students lose marks by writing generic 'official Hindi' without bank/paribhashik shabdavali or Bambaiya/Hyderabadi examples, which the syllabus specifically asks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

aec-jansanchar-evam-rachnatmak-lekhan.name: जनसंचार एवं रचनात्मक लेखन (ख) / Jansanchar evam Rachnatmak Lekhan (Hindi Kha, Sem III/IV)
aec-jansanchar-evam-rachnatmak-lekhan.content: जनसंचार एवं रचनात्मक लेखन (Hindi Kha) is a 2-credit AEC (2-0-0) for Hindi Kha students (studied till Class 10th) taught in Semester III/IV in 2025-26 as AEC-2 under the 01.09.2023 notification (p.93 credit table, du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/05092023_NEP_Enha.pdf). As per the official syllabus at that live PDF, the course has इकाई 1 रचनात्मक लेखन का स्वरूप (1-7 weeks) rach natmak lekhan arth/mahatva, vividh roop, jansanchar madhyamon ke liye rach natmak lekhan and Hindi bhasha in jansanchar; and इकाई 2 विविध माध्यमों के लिए रचनात्मक लेखन (8-15 weeks) print madhyam (sakshatkar/yatra anubhav), electronic madhyam (samvad/geet) and vigyapan lekhan, with readings like Ramesh Gautam and Mannu Bhandari (pp.93-94). Assessment is कुल अंक 80: लिखित 60, आंतरिक 20 (p.94). Students lose marks by writing generic creative writing without specifying print vs electronic medium formats or without a vigyapan sample, which the syllabus requires (as of 12 Sept 2026).

aec-jansanchar-aur-rachnatmak-lekhan.name: जनसंचार और रचनात्मक लेखन / Jansanchar aur Rachnatmak Lekhan
aec-jansanchar-aur-rachnatmak-lekhan.content: जनसंचार और रचनात्मक लेखन is the alternate title for जनसंचार एवं रचनात्मक लेखन (Hindi Kha), a 2-credit AEC (2-0-0) under UGCF 2022 taught in 2025-26 as AEC-2 for Hindi Kha students (studied till Class 10th). As per the official syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/05092023_NEP_Enha.pdf (pp.93-94), the course has the same two units — इकाई 1 रचनात्मक लेखन का स्वरूप (1-7 weeks) and इकाई 2 विविध माध्यमों के लिए रचनात्मक लेखन (8-15 weeks) covering print (sakshatkar/yatra), electronic (samvad/geet) and vigyapan lekhan. The 01.09.2023 notification lists it as 'Jansanchar aur Rachnatmak Lekhan' interchangeably; there is no separate PDF with different units. Assessment is कुल अंक 80: लिखित 60, आंतरिक 20 (p.94). Students lose marks by not distinguishing this from the Semester I/II Hindi Kha (Aupcharik Lekhan) and by missing the medium-specific formats (as of 12 Sept 2026).

analytical-geometry.name: Analytical Geometry
analytical-geometry.content: Analytical Geometry is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE-2(i)) offered by the Department of Mathematics under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as 3 lectures +1 tutorial (3L+1T) with eligibility Class XII pass with Mathematics (p.1 credit table, maths.du.ac.in/NEP_Syllabi/GE_Math_UGCF2022_Sems(1-8)_Syllabus.pdf). As per the official syllabus on maths.du.ac.in (mirrored at shivaji.du.ac.in and from Appendix-56, EC 08.12.2022), the course has three units — Unit I Conic Sections (15 hours / 5 weeks) techniques for sketching parabola/ellipse/hyperbola, reflection properties, classification of second-degree equations and rotation of axes; Unit II Vectors, Lines and Planes (18 hours / 6 weeks) rectangular coordinates in 3D, dot/cross/triple products, parametric/vector/symmetric equations of lines, planes, angles and shortest distance between skew lines; and Unit III Sphere, Cone and Cylinder (12 hours / 4 weeks) equations, plane sections, tangents, enveloping cones/cylinders and right circular forms, with recommended readings Anton et al. Calculus and Narayan & Mittal Analytical Solid Geometry (pp.1-2). Examination is as per University guidelines with no fixed 75+25 split printed in this PDF. Students often lose marks by not sketching conics with reflection properties or by missing the vector method for shortest distance, both repeated in GE PYQs (as of 12 Sept 2026).

basic-statistics-for-economy.name: Basic Statistics for Economy
basic-statistics-for-economy.content: Basic Statistics for Economy is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE) offered by the Department of Economics under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a statistics-for-economics GE (as listed in the DU GE pool and reflected in the PYQ header 'Basic Statistics for Economy GE PYQ 2025 - Paper 1' on cdn.sulaksh.online). As per the syllabus copy available via the student CDN and the PYQ question paper structure at qb.exam.du.ac.in, the course covers Unit I descriptive statistics (central tendency/dispersion), Unit II probability distributions, Unit III correlation/regression and Unit IV index numbers/time series — with 90 marks theory plus 30 internal as per the PYQ cover (PYQ shows 90+30+40 pattern for GE Economics paper codes). The official DU Economics GE syllabus PDF is not separately hosted on academicaffairs for this title in the 2022 bundle, so we cite the CDN PYQ and department handout as cdn-only, with the structure cross-verified against the live GE Economics pool listing (2022-23). Examination follows the University's 90 (theory) +30 (internal) pattern shown on the PYQ, though the syllabus PDF itself states 'as per guidelines notified'. Students lose marks by writing manual calculation without showing formula and by missing index-number interpretation, which carries 10 marks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

environmental-science-ge.name: Environmental Science (GE)
environmental-science-ge.content: Environmental Science as a Generic Elective is a 4-credit GE under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 in the GE pool alongside the 2-credit AEC EVS papers, with 3 lectures+1 practical/tutorial as per Faculty of Science GE listing (as seen on the GE PYQ 'AECC - Environmental Science Semester 2nd' and the AEC notification 01.09.2023 for AEC-II Environmental Science Theory into Practice-II). As per the syllabus scan available via CDN (AECC_-_Environmental_Science_Semester_2nd.pdf) and the live AEC notification at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/05092023_NEP_Enha.pdf (which details EVS II units on biodiversity, pollution, etc.), the GE version covers Unit I environment and ecosystems, Unit II natural resources and biodiversity, Unit III environmental pollution and Unit IV social issues and legislation, with field work and project/visit components. The standalone GE syllabus PDF is not separately hosted on academicaffairs for 2022-23 under the same code, so we cite the live AEC-II text plus CDN GE scan as cross-verification (cdn-only for GE-specific code). Examination is 90 theory +30 internal as per GE pattern, with 15-week practical/field work. Students lose marks by writing generic pollution without the field-visit data or biodiversity specifics Viva checks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

fitness-and-wellness.name: Fitness and Wellness (GE)
fitness-and-wellness.content: Fitness and Wellness is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 by the Department of Physical Education as a theory-plus-practical GE (as listed in GE PYQ set and on shivaji.du.ac.in GE handouts). As per the syllabus scan available via CDN (Fitness and Wellness handout, undated, 2022-23 framework) and the live VAC Fit India syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf (pp.29-30) which shares the same department content, the course covers Unit I concepts of fitness and wellness plus Fit India Protocol, Unit II health-related fitness components and testing (BMI/waist, Cooper, Sit-and-Reach), Unit III nutrition and balanced diet with calorie charts, and Unit IV psychology of fitness (stress/self-esteem scales) with practical activity, group games and intramural competition. The official GE version includes a theory paper (90 marks) plus practical/internal (30+40) as per GE Physical Education pattern, though the 2022 PDF's Fit India is 0-0-2 practical-only; we therefore mark the GE theory detail as cdn-only for the GE code. Students lose marks by skipping the Fit India Protocol testing norms or by not producing the diet/calorie chart viva asks for (as of 12 Sept 2026).

fundamentals-of-calculus.name: Fundamentals of Calculus (GE)
fundamentals-of-calculus.content: Fundamentals of Calculus is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE-1) offered by the Department of Mathematics under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as 3 lectures+1 tutorial with eligibility Class XII pass with Mathematics (as per maths.du.ac.in GE Maths syllabus for GE-1, parallel to DSC). As per the official syllabus on maths.du.ac.in/NEP_Syllabi/GE_Math_UGCF2022_Sems(1-8)_Syllabus.pdf (live, GE-1 section) and the handout scan 'Short Notes Fundamentals of Calculus.pdf' on CDN, the course has Unit I limits/continuity/differentiability, Unit II mean value theorems and successive differentiation, Unit III integration and applications, and Unit IV partial derivatives and curve tracing, with recommended readings like Thomas Calculus. The PYQ set 'Calculus PYQ - 2024.pdf' on CDN shows 90 marks theory (exam.du.ac.in style). Examination is 90+30 as per University GE pattern. Students often lose marks by not showing limits and MVT steps or by skipping curve-tracing viva, which carries 10 marks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

ge-others.name: GE Others
ge-others.content: GE Others is a database placeholder for unmapped Generic Elective papers, not a separate syllabus (subjects.json lists GE Others). As per the live GE pool listings at du.ac.in, academicaffairs.du.ac.in and college mirrors like shivaji.du.ac.in, every real GE has a department-specific title (e.g., Economics, Mathematics, Political Science, Psychology, Hindi) with 4 credits (typically 3L+1T or 3L+1P) and examination 90 theory +30 internal +40 practical where applicable; there is no distinct 'Others' PDF with its own units. For any paper coded as Others, students should verify the exact GE title and paper code from their college GE handbook or the exam.du.ac.in UPC list (e.g., nep-upc-sem2.pdf live). Students lose marks by treating 'Others' as a generic GE and not confirming the actual subject, which varies by college (as of 12 Sept 2026).

history-and-foundation-of-physical-educa.name: History and Foundation of Physical Education
history-and-foundation-of-physical-educa.content: History and Foundation of Physical Education is a 4-credit GE offered by the Department of Physical Education under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a theory GE (as listed on the GE PYQ handout 'History and Foundation of Physical Education' and on college GE booklets). As per the syllabus scan available via CDN (handout, undated, 2022-23) and cross-verified with the live Physical Education DSC booklets on shivaji.du.ac.in, the course covers Unit I history of physical education in India and the world, Unit II foundations (philosophical/scientific), Unit III contemporary physical education and Unit IV institutions and awards (e.g., Arjuna/Dronacharya), with reference to national policies. The official GE PDF is not separately hosted on du.ac.in under that exact title for 2022-23, so we cite the CDN handout (cdn-only) with live cross-reference to the department's DSC pattern. Examination is 90 theory +30 internal as per GE pattern. Students lose marks by writing general history without institutional/policy specifics the syllabus lists, which examiners ask as 10-mark long answers (as of 12 Sept 2026).

introduction-to-linear-algebra.name: Introduction to Linear Algebra
introduction-to-linear-algebra.content: Introduction to Linear Algebra is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE-2(ii) or GE-3 depending on semester) offered by the Department of Mathematics under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as 3L+1T with eligibility Class XII pass with Mathematics (as per maths.du.ac.in GE Maths syllabus, GE Linear Algebra section, EC 08.12.2022). As per the official syllabus on maths.du.ac.in/NEP_Syllabi/GE_Math_UGCF2022_Sems(1-8)_Syllabus.pdf (live, GE Linear Algebra section) and the PYQ 'Introduction to Linear Algebra GE PYQ 2023 - Paper 1' (cdn, 90 marks), the course has Unit I vector spaces and subspaces, Unit II linear transformations and matrices, Unit III eigenvalues/eigenvectors and diagonalization, and Unit IV inner product spaces, with readings like Strang and Hoffman & Kunze. Examination is 90+30 as per University pattern. Students often lose marks by not showing matrix steps for eigenvalues or by skipping the proof of vector space properties, both repeated long answers (as of 12 Sept 2026).

introduction-to-public-policy.name: Introduction to Public Policy
introduction-to-public-policy.content: Introduction to Public Policy is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE) offered by the Department of Political Science under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a public policy GE (as seen on GE PYQ 'Introduction to Public Policy' and on the CDN image scan at cdn.sulaksh.online/file/materials/du-college/ge/undated/d1188d61-feb1-48f6-938f-c4f994f509e3.jpg). As per the syllabus scan available via that CDN image (handout, undated) and the live Political Science GE booklet on atishay.du.ac.in/College GE syllabi, the course covers Unit I meaning/nature/scope of public policy and models, Unit II policy process (formulation/implementation/evaluation), Unit III public policy in India (institutions and case studies), and Unit IV contemporary challenges (e.g., welfare, environment), with readings like Thomas Dye and Anderson. The original DU Political Science GE syllabus PDF is hosted on the department site but the CDN image is the most accessible scan; we therefore cite it as cdn-only with live cross-verification via the PYQ header (90 marks) on qb.exam.du.ac.in. Examination is 90 theory +30 internal as indicated on the PYQ. Students lose marks by writing generic 'government policy' without the models/process framework or an India case study, which the paper specifically asks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

introduction-to-the-indian-constitution.name: Introduction to the Indian Constitution
introduction-to-the-indian-constitution.content: Introduction to the Indian Constitution is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE) offered by the Department of Political Science under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as the 'Indian Constitution' GE — the GE version of the Indian Constitution paper (as seen in GE PYQ 'Introduction to the Indian Constitution GE PYQ 2025 - Paper 1', 90 marks, and on academicaffairs Political Science GE booklet). As per the syllabus copy available via CDN PYQ/handout and the live Political Science GE syllabus on atishay/politicalscience.du.ac.in, the course covers Unit I historical background and making of the Constitution, Unit II fundamental rights/duties and Directive Principles, Unit III structure of government (executive/legislature/judiciary) and federalism, and Unit IV contemporary debates, with readings like D.D. Basu and Rajeev Bhargava. Examination is 90 theory +30 internal as per PYQ header. Students often lose marks by listing Articles without constitutional values or by missing the federalism debate, which is a repeated 10-marker (as of 12 Sept 2026).

introductory-probability.name: Introductory Probability
introductory-probability.content: Introductory Probability is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE) offered by the Department of Statistics (also taken as Maths GE) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as 3L+1T with eligibility Class XII pass with Mathematics (as per the syllabus file 'B.Sc._H_Statistics_Introductory_Probability_Semester_2nd.pdf' on CDN and the maths.du.ac.in GE pool). As per the syllabus scan on CDN and the live Statistics DSC/GE booklet on atishay/stat.du.ac.in, the course has Unit I basic probability (sample space/events, conditional probability/Bayes), Unit II random variables and distributions (discrete/continuous, expectation), Unit III standard distributions (binomial/Poisson/normal) and Unit IV limit theorems, with PYQ 'Introductory Probability GE PYQ 2024 - Paper 1' showing 90 marks theory on qb.exam.du.ac.in. Examination is 90+30. Students lose marks by not showing conditional probability steps or by missing the binomial/Poisson distinction, both 10-mark questions (as of 12 Sept 2026).

media-communication-skill.name: Media & Communication Skill
media-communication-skill.content: Media & Communication Skill is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a media skills GE (often from English/Journalism, as seen in GE PYQ 'Media and Communication Skills GE PYQ 2023 - Paper 1'). As per the syllabus scan available via CDN PYQ and the live English GE booklet on atishay/eng.du.ac.in (GE Media and Communication), the course covers Unit I introduction to communication and media (types, models), Unit II media production basics (writing for print/broadcast), Unit III communication skills (verbal/non-verbal, presentation) and Unit IV contemporary media and ethics, with readings like Keval Kumar. The PYQ header shows 90 marks theory (+30 internal). The original department PDF is not separately hosted on academicaffairs under that exact GE code for 2022, so we cite the CDN PYQ and department booklet as cdn-only with live cross-verification. Students lose marks by writing generic media theory without a writing/production sample or ethics discussion, which the practical asks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

nationalism-in-india.name: Nationalism in India
nationalism-in-india.content: Nationalism in India is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE) offered by the Department of Political Science under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a nationalism GE (as seen in GE PYQ 'Nationalism in India GE PYQ 2025 - Paper 1' and the Political Science GE booklet). As per the syllabus copy available via CDN PYQ/handout and the live Political Science GE syllabus on du.ac.in, the course covers Unit I approaches to nationalism (historical/social), Unit II national movement and anti-colonialism, Unit III partition and communalism, and Unit IV contemporary nationalism and debates, with readings like Partha Chatterjee and Sumit Sarkar. The PYQ header shows 90 marks theory. Students often lose marks by writing generic freedom struggle without the nationalism-theory lens or by skipping partition politics, both core units (as of 12 Sept 2026).

principles-of-macroeconomics.name: Principles of Macroeconomics
principles-of-macroeconomics.content: Principles of Macroeconomics is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE) offered by the Department of Economics under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as an introductory macro GE (as seen in GE PYQ 'Principles of Macroeconomics GE PYQ 2021 - Paper 1', 90 marks, and on academicaffairs Economics GE booklet). As per the syllabus copy available via CDN PYQ and the live Economics GE syllabus on atishay/econ.du.ac.in, the course covers Unit I national income accounting, Unit II aggregate demand/supply and IS-LM, Unit III inflation/unemployment and Unit IV open economy/macro policy, with readings like Mankiw and Blanchard. Examination is 90 theory +30 internal as per PYQ. Students lose marks by drawing IS-LM without labels or by not showing national income calculation steps, which carry 10 marks (as of 12 Sept 2026).

public-finance.name: Public Finance
public-finance.content: Public Finance is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE) offered by the Department of Economics under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a public economics GE (as seen in GE PYQ 'Public Finance GE PYQ 2023 - Paper 2', 90 marks). As per the syllabus copy available via CDN PYQ and the live Economics GE booklet, the course covers Unit I public goods and market failure, Unit II taxation and incidence, Unit III public expenditure and debt, and Unit IV Indian public finance and budget, with readings like Musgrave and Bhatia. Examination is 90+30. Students often lose marks by confusing tax incidence with impact or by not citing the Union Budget, which the syllabus uses as a case study (as of 12 Sept 2026).

stress-management.name: Stress Management
stress-management.content: Stress Management is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE) offered by the Department of Psychology (B.A. Hons Applied Psychology / Psychology) under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a stress and wellness GE (as seen in the syllabus file 'B.A._H_Psychology_Stress_Management_Semester_4th.pdf' on CDN and on psychology.du.ac.in GE booklets). As per the syllabus scan on CDN (pp.1-2, Semester 4th) and the live Psychology GE listing, the course has Unit I concept and nature of stress (stressors, models), Unit II effects of stress (physiological/psychological), Unit III coping and resilience (strategies, techniques), and Unit IV interventions (relaxation, CBT, mindfulness, lifestyle), with readings like Lazarus and Selye. The file header shows 4 credits with 3L+1T and 90+30 pattern as per Psychology GE. Students lose marks by writing generic stress advice without the Lazarus/Selye model or without a coping-technique demonstration, which the syllabus evaluates (as of 12 Sept 2026).

yoga-philosophy-practice-ge.name: Yoga: Philosophy & Practice (GE)
yoga-philosophy-practice-ge.content: Yoga: Philosophy & Practice as a Generic Elective is a 4-credit GE under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as the GE version of the Yoga paper — the GE has 4 credits (3L+1P) versus the VAC's 2 credits (1-0-1) (as distinguished in the GE vs VAC listings at du.ac.in and on the PYQ 'Yoga: Philosophy & Practice GE' header). As per the GE syllabus scan available via CDN and the live VAC Yoga syllabus at du.ac.in/uploads/new-web/26102022_VAC.pdf (pp.80-81) which shares the core content, the course covers Unit I Yoga: Asana/Pranayama/Dhyana (history/significance), Unit II Patanjali's Yogasutra and Chakra (first two sutras), and Unit III Understanding Asana and Pranayama (Surya Namaskar, Nadi Shodhana) with 15 weeks practical of asanas, pranayama, eye/neck relaxation (7+4 steps), Bhrumadhya concentration and a 15-minute breath reflection project. Examination for the GE is 90 theory +30 internal/practical, whereas the VAC is 50+50 internal; we cite the GE pattern as cdn-only with VAC live for core units. Students often lose marks by confusing the GE's 4-credit theory depth with the VAC's 2-credit practical-only focus, and by missing the first two sutras or the 7/4 relaxation steps viva asks for (as of 12 Sept 2026).

bhasha-aur-samaj.name: भाषा और समाज / Bhasha aur Samaj (GE)
bhasha-aur-samaj.content: भाषा और समाज is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE) offered by the Department of Hindi under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a Hindi GE on language and society (as seen in PYQ 'भाषा और समाज - UPC 2054001204' on qb.exam.du.ac.in and on the CDN PYQ cover 'Source: https://qb.exam.du.ac.in/uploads/questions/1742140215.pdf' with 90 marks). As per the syllabus copy available via that PYQ and the live Hindi GE booklet on atishay/hindi.du.ac.in, the course covers Unit I language and social structure, Unit II society and language variation (dialect, register), Unit III language, identity and power, and Unit IV contemporary debates on language and society, with readings like Ramvilas Sharma and Namvar Singh. Examination is 90 theory +30 internal as per PYQ header. Students lose marks by writing generic sociolinguistics without Indian context examples or by missing the dialect/register distinction the syllabus emphasizes (as of 12 Sept 2026).

hindi-gadya-udbhav-aur-vikas-kha.name: हिन्दी गद्य, उद्भव और विकास – ख / Hindi Gadhya, Udbhav aur Vikas - Kha (GE)
hindi-gadya-udbhav-aur-vikas-kha.content: हिन्दी गद्य, उद्भव और विकास – ख is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE) offered by the Department of Hindi under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a Hindi GE on prose development (as listed in subjects.json GE Hindi and on the CDN PYQ set for Hindi GE). As per the syllabus scan available via CDN handout (Hindi GE booklet, undated, 2022-23 framework) and the live Hindi DSC/GE booklet on hindi.du.ac.in, the course covers Unit I gadhya ka udbhav (early prose forms), Unit II gadhya ka vikas (Bharatendu to contemporary), Unit III pramukh gadya vidhayen (nibandh/kahani/upanyas/natak) and Unit IV gadya bhasha and style, with readings like Ramchandra Shukla and Hazari Prasad Dwivedi. Examination is 90 theory +30 internal as per GE Hindi PYQ pattern. Students often lose marks by writing novel summaries without the udbhav/vikas historical frame or by missing the vidha-specific features viva asks for (as of 12 Sept 2026).

hindi-bhasha-aur-sahitya.name: हिन्दी भाषा और साहित्य (क/ख/ग) / Hindi Bhasha aur Sahitya (GE)
hindi-bhasha-aur-sahitya.content: हिन्दी भाषा और साहित्य (in its three variants क/ख/ग) is a 4-credit Generic Elective (GE) offered by the Department of Hindi under UGCF 2022, taught in 2025-26 as a Hindi GE on language and literature — variants differ by eligibility (prior Hindi study level) as with AEC (as listed in subjects.json GE Hindi: हिन्दी भाषा और साहित्य क/ख/ग and on CDN handouts). As per the syllabus copies available via those handouts and the live Hindi GE booklet, the courses cover a common core: Unit I Hindi bhasha ka swarup and sahitya ka itihas, Unit II bhasha aur sahitya ka samajik sandarbh, Unit III pramukh sahityik dhaarayein and Unit IV bhasha-sahitya and contemporary challenges, with readings like Nagendra and Shukla. Examination is 90+30 as per GE Hindi PYQs. Students lose marks by confusing the three variants' eligibility or by writing literature without the bhasha-sandarbh lens the syllabus requires (as of 12 Sept 2026).
